column5: Project selection finalized. Team roles assigned (PM: Margulies, Hardware: Mejia/Orozco, CV: Kelly, Web: Hong). Initial project scope defined. Began system architecture research.
Researched IR break-beam sensors, piezo vibration detection, Raspberry Pi 5 capabilities, and OpenCV for basketball tracking. Began drafting system block diagram.
Completed system architecture definition. Subsystem responsibilities finalized. Selected ESP32 as sensor controller. Confirmed Rust for Raspberry Pi software stack.
Completed block diagram and subsystem interface definitions. Drafted component list and initial BOM. Finalized data flow: ESP32 ? Pi ? Tailscale ? Flask ? hoopiq.shop.
Subsystem designs finalized. Hardware orders submitted through university procurement (ESP32, IR sensors, piezo discs, ADC, resistors, wiring). Pi environment setup began.
Component orders placed. Raspberry Pi 5 received and initial OS setup completed. Rust toolchain and Cargo build environment configured. Placeholder camera testing started.
University procurement orders delayed. Critical sensors (IR, piezo, ESP32) not yet received. Team members began purchasing components out-of-pocket to prevent timeline slip.
column7: University procurement significantly slower than anticipated. Out-of-pocket purchases made by team.

column5: Shifted focus to software while awaiting parts. Designed serial packet format (EVENT_TYPE,TIMESTAMP,IR_FLAG,PIEZO_FLAG). Researched MOG2 background subtraction. Drafted ESP32 firmware state machine architecture.
column7: Pivot to software-first development to use downtime productively.

column5: OpenCV integration tested on Pi using placeholder video. Rust Arc/Mutex shared state model designed. ESP32 firmware ISR and threshold logic written and reviewed off-device.
Remaining out-of-pocket hardware components arrived. Began breadboard prototyping of ESP32 + IR sensor pair. Verified 3.3V IR emitter operation. Initial piezo readings captured.
ESP32 firmware compiled and flashed. IR beam break detection confirmed. Piezo threshold calibration begun. GPIO pin mapping finalized (GPIO 27: IR, GPIO 32/35: piezo backboard, GPIO 34: piezo rim).
Shot event state machine implemented: MAKE, SWISH, RIM_CONTACT, MISS classification. Dynamic baseline filtering added to piezo firmware. Serial packet transmission to Pi tested with synthetic events.
Mini-hoop prototype assembled. IR beam physically mounted across rim plane. Piezos mounted to backboard and rim. Wired serial confirmed from ESP32 to Pi. Rust serial parser implemented on Pi side.
Thanksgiving week. Threshold tuning continued. Camera mounted and initial ball detection tested using MOG2. Dual-stream FFmpeg/v4l2loopback architecture prototyped. Tailscale account configured.
column7: Thanksgiving — reduced availability but continued progress.

column5: Full end-to-end proof-of-concept assembled. ESP32 detecting shots and transmitting to Pi. Pi parsing serial events. Flask backend skeleton deployed on Render. Dashboard prototype running at hoopiq.shop.

Proof-of-concept demonstration completed. All subsystems functional at baseline level: sensor detection, serial comm, Pi processing, cloud backend, and dashboard. Semester 1 concluded. Report submitted.
column7: Proof-of-concept successfully demonstrated. Strong foundation heading into 490B.

column5: Semester 2 kickoff. Hardware team began refining hoop sensor mounting configuration. Reviewed Semester 1 lessons learned. Updated project plan and set Demo 1 target for Week 4.

IR beam alignment adjusted for more reliable shot detection. Piezo sensor mounting positions iterated — tested left, center, and right backboard placement for optimal vibration response. Wiring stabilized with cable management.

Finalized sensor mounting configuration on backboard. Full hardware assembly stabilized with mechanical fasteners. Sensor alignment re-verified post-mounting. Demo 1 test runs performed: 100% make detection, 100% rim contact.

Demo 1 completed. ESP32-based shot detection demonstrated. IR + piezo dual-sensor event classification confirmed operational. Make detection: 3/3 (100%). Rim contact: 2/2 (100%). Serial comm to Pi stable.
column7: Demo 1: PASS. All targets met or exceeded.

column5: Computer vision pipeline development accelerated. MOG2 background subtraction refined. Ball contour filtering tuned (area + aspect ratio constraints). Rolling position buffer implemented for trajectory smoothing.

Shot zone classification implemented: Left Corner 3, Right Corner 3, Above Break 3, Paint, Mid-Range. Arc height calculation (peak Y relative to release point) and entry angle estimation implemented. AHEAD of planned milestone.
column7: Shot zone classification and arc/angle features completed ahead of schedule.

column5: Heatmap visualization implemented in dashboard. Airball classification logic added on Pi side (5-second timeout from detected shot attempt). CSV session export added to dashboard. All three stretch goals completed.
column7: Stretch goals (zone, heatmap, export) all completed by Week 7 — well ahead of plan.

column5: End-to-end data pipeline validated: ESP32 event ? serial ? Pi Rust binary ? Tailscale tunnel ? Render Flask API ? hoopiq.shop dashboard. Latency confirmed under 1 second. Dual-stream RTSP confirmed stable.

Demo 2 preparation. Ball detection validated under varied lighting. Trajectory overlay confirmed rendering on dashboard. WebRTC/WHEP stream confirmed accessible from external browser. System stability tested over extended session.

Demo 2 completed. Live ball detection and dual-stream camera architecture demonstrated. Logitech C922x ? Rust+OpenCV processing stream + RTSP broadcast both operational. Ball trajectory overlay confirmed live on dashboard.
column7: Demo 2: PASS. CV subsystem met all planned targets.

column5: Flask backend on Render validated with full session data flow. Dashboard displaying shot log, statistics, shot type breakdown, shooting percentage, heatmap, and zone percentages. Real-time API polling confirmed.
Session management, counter reset, and export functionality validated end-to-end. Dashboard UI polished. API endpoint error handling added. Render deployment confirmed stable under continuous use.

Demo 3 completed. Backend + dashboard integration demonstrated with mock and live data. Shot log, stats, heatmap, and CSV export all confirmed functional. Real-time data flow from Render to hoopiq.shop confirmed.
column7: Demo 3: PASS. All dashboard targets met.

column5: All subsystems integrated simultaneously in real-world shooting conditions. Latency measured end-to-end (sensor event to dashboard update). System stability tested over 30+ minutes of continuous operation. Dashboard UI final polish begun.

Final three weeks of integration and cleanup completed. Dashboard fully polished and stabilized for expo. Hoop sensor, Pi, Tailscale tunnel, Flask backend, and hoopiq.shop all confirmed running simultaneously. Demo 4 dry runs completed.
column7: Final system state confirmed ready for Demo 4 and Expo.
